method: One dossier per saved watchlist ticker plus this week's curated ideas. Conviction is capped at 3 for names that are not yet consistently profitable, and that cap is stated in the bear case. Levels come from the real Fri 2026-09-04 close and 52-week range; sell > buy > stop throughout.

ALAB.why: Jumped 9.75% on Friday to 310.40 while the S&P fell 0.38% - the strongest large-cap move outside memory - and still trades 37.9% below its 499.48 52-week high. The bounce came off recent lows, so this is a recovery attempt rather than a confirmed trend.
bull: Rose 9.75% on Friday against a falling index.
Connectivity content per rack rises with AI rack density - Dell's $95bn backlog is the demand proxy.
37.9% below the 52-week high leaves substantial repair room.
bear: A single 9.75% session off a low is a bounce, not a base.
Small-cap volatility: the 52-week range runs from 97.89 to 499.48.
Customer concentration in a handful of AI system builders.
ALAB.inv: If it gives back Friday's 9.75% and makes a new low, the recovery has failed.
ALAB.thesis: Connectivity silicon (retimers, CXL) that sits between accelerators and memory in an AI rack. Content per rack rises as rack density rises, which is exactly what Dell's record $95.0bn AI-server backlog implies.

APLD.why: Rose 1.78% on Friday to 26.37 but lagged the neocloud complex badly, where NBIS rose 7.48%, IREN 7.27% and CRWV 5.68%. It trades 48.0% below its 50.73 52-week high.
bull: Power-rich sites with existing interconnects are the scarce input for AI data centres.
48.0% below the 52-week high.
Rose 1.78% on Friday in a red tape.
bear: Lagged every neocloud peer on the strongest day the theme has had in weeks - conviction capped at 3 as it is not consistently profitable.
Development-stage capex is debt-funded, and the 30-year sits at 5.243%.
48.0% below the high with no base formed.
APLD.inv: Failure to convert development sites into signed hosting contracts leaves it with capex and no revenue.
APLD.thesis: Data-centre developer converting power-rich sites into AI hosting capacity - the asset is the interconnect, not the building.

ASML.why: A monopoly with a two-year order lag on everything the AI build-out announces. Every fab TSMC and Micron commit to this year is an ASML tool order in 2028. It closed Friday at 1,714.88, 14.3% under its high, on a 4.17% bounce.
bull: Absolute monopoly in EUV - there is no second supplier at any price.
Every fab expansion announced during this AI cycle converts into ASML bookings with a lag.
14.3% below the 52-week high while the customers it sells to make new highs.
bear: Bookings are violently lumpy; one deferred shipment moves the quarter and the stock.
China export controls remain a live restriction on a meaningful revenue slice.
No smart-money signal at all this week - nobody with an information edge is buying it here.
ASML.inv: A capex pause at TSMC or Samsung, or tightened export controls, removes the order visibility the multiple depends on.
ASML.thesis: the only company on earth that makes EUV lithography machines. Trailing FCF of $11.5bn on 387m shares with $8.7bn net cash. Revenue is lumpy because tool shipments are lumpy, but the order book is the leading indicator for every fab expansion announced anywhere.

AVGO.why: The single widest gap in the book between what the business printed and what the tape pays for it. Broadcom just guided AI revenue to $58bn this year, $115bn next and $230bn in FY28, and the shares still sit 27.7% below their 52-week high at 357.90. You are being paid to wait for the multiple to catch up to the disclosure.
bull: FY28 AI revenue framed at $230bn against $58bn this year - if even two-thirds lands, today's 357.90 is a fraction of fair value.
Six XPU customers named including OpenAI and Anthropic; custom accelerators are multi-year programmes, not spot orders.
27.7% below the 495.00 52-week high while earnings compound at +86% - the de-rating is a multiple story, not a business story.
bear: Customer concentration is extreme: a single hyperscaler pushing an XPU programme out a year would gut the FY27 bridge.
The 5-yr Treasury printed a fresh 52-week high at 4.545% on Friday - long-duration growth multiples keep compressing while the curve does that.
Guiding AI revenue three years out invites a miss; the market has already shown it will de-rate first and check later.
AVGO.inv: If AI revenue growth decelerates below ~100% y/y or a named XPU customer exits, the FY27/FY28 bridge breaks and the thesis is void.
AVGO.thesis: Q3 FY26 on Sep 2 printed $29.6bn revenue, +86% y/y, with operating income up 92% and adjusted EPS $3.32 vs $3.24 consensus. AI semiconductor revenue alone was $16.7bn, +221% y/y, across six XPU customers including Google, OpenAI and Anthropic. Custom-silicon design wins are multi-year and sticky, and the VMware software base funds the buyback.

BSX.why: Four insiders put $9.49m of their own money into this at $48.26 on Aug 25, and it closed Friday at 47.80 - 1.0% below their price. It rose 1.81% on a day healthcare fell 1.04% as a sector. A 56.3% drawdown with a four-person insider cluster underneath it is the clearest risk/reward setup in this book.
bull: Four insiders bought $9.49m at $48.26 on Aug 25 - it closed Friday 1.0% below their price.
Rose 1.81% on Friday while healthcare was the second-worst sector at -1.04%.
56.3% below the 52-week high on a device business whose procedure volumes grow with demographics.
bear: A 56.3% drawdown of that magnitude usually reflects something real - insiders can be early and wrong.
Only 13.3% above the 52-week low; the downtrend has not been broken on the chart.
Healthcare as a sector is out of favour and fell 1.04% on Friday.
BSX.inv: A break below the 42.20 52-week low would mean the insider cluster was wrong about the bottom - exit rather than average down.
BSX.thesis: a medical-device business with a strong electrophysiology franchise and consistent procedure-volume-driven growth. Devices are less exposed to patent cliffs than pharmaceuticals, and the revenue base compounds with an ageing population rather than with the economy.

CCJ.why: Fuel for the nuclear reactors everyone wants built, with the Westinghouse stake adding reactor services on top. It has reclaimed $100 but was flat on Friday while the generators bounced 3-5%, so the market is expressing the nuclear theme through power sellers rather than through fuel right now.
bull: Largest Western uranium producer with long-term utility contracts providing revenue visibility.
The Westinghouse stake adds reactor services to fuel supply.
Reclaimed the $100 level after losing it during the August de-rating.
bear: Flat on Friday while CEG rose 4.88% - the nuclear bid is not reaching the fuel layer.
25.5% below the 52-week high with no company-specific catalyst.
Uranium spot prices are thin and volatile; the equity moves more than the commodity.
CCJ.inv: If the nuclear equity bid keeps bypassing the fuel names, the sector rotation is happening without you and the position has no edge.
CCJ.thesis: the largest Western uranium producer, with the Westinghouse stake giving it exposure to reactor services as well as fuel. Long-term contracts with utilities provide revenue visibility that spot uranium prices alone would not.

CEG.why: AI power has been the weakest theme in this book for a month, and it just put in its strongest session - up 4.88% on a day the S&P fell. The contracted base is real: 20-year agreements with Microsoft for Crane and Meta for 1,121MW at Clinton turn merchant nuclear into something closer to a utility.
bull: Rose 4.88% on Friday while the S&P fell 0.38% - the strongest relative session AI-power has had in weeks.
20-year Microsoft (Crane, 835MW) and Meta (Clinton, 1,121MW) agreements are contracted, not merchant.
27.6% below the 52-week high after a sustained de-rating - the risk/reward has improved with the price.
bear: A 22.4x forward multiple against Vistra's 14.4x for a similar asset base is hard to defend.
Rate-sensitive: the 30-year at 5.243% is what caused the de-rating and it has not reversed.
One 4.88% day off a base is a bounce until it is confirmed; this theme has bounced and failed before.
CEG.inv: If the long end keeps rising and no new contracted agreement is announced, the de-rating resumes and the bounce was noise.
CEG.thesis: the largest nuclear fleet in the United States, with 20-year contracted agreements - Microsoft for the 835MW Crane restart and Meta for 1,121MW from Clinton - that convert merchant power into utility-like contracted revenue. It trades around 22.4x forward earnings, a premium to Vistra's roughly 14.4x.

CRWD.why: Closed at 213.10, down 0.87%, 8.9% below its 233.88 52-week high - the shallowest drawdown in the security sleeve, which is a relative-strength signal in a week when Zscaler fell 4.5% despite eight price-target raises.
bull: Only 8.9% below its 52-week high while Zscaler sits 49.6% below its own - clear relative strength.
Data network effect across the endpoint fleet compounds detection quality.
Security budgets are the last IT line item to be cut.
bear: 8.9% off the high means limited discount; you are paying for the relative strength.
The whole security sector is being punished for good news right now.
No smart-money filing supports it this week.
CRWD.inv: If CRWD starts fading upgrades the way ZS did on Friday, the relative-strength edge is gone.
CRWD.thesis: Endpoint security platform with the best data network effect in the sector - every endpoint improves detection for every other endpoint.

CRWV.why: Rose 5.68% on Friday to 89.36 with the rest of the AI-infrastructure complex, but remains 41.7% below its 153.20 52-week high - the deepest drawdown among the neoclouds here.
bull: Rose 5.68% on Friday while the S&P fell 0.38%.
Contracted capacity with named AI customers gives more revenue visibility than spot GPU rental.
41.7% below the 52-week high - the most repair room in the neocloud group.
bear: Not consistently profitable and heavily leveraged to fund GPU purchases - conviction capped at 3.
41.7% below the high means the market has repeatedly rejected higher prices.
Debt-funded GPU capex is punished hard whenever the long end rises, and the 30-year sits at 5.243%.
CRWV.inv: A contract cancellation from a major customer, or an inability to refinance GPU capex, breaks the model.
CRWV.thesis: The largest dedicated AI cloud, renting NVIDIA capacity at scale on long-term contracts. Heavily capital-intensive and not yet consistently profitable.

DE.why: Two upgrades in one week - Baird to Outperform at $800, Evercore ISI to Outperform at $813 - on a stock making its 25th new high in twelve months. Precision agriculture is quietly turning a cyclical machinery business into a recurring-revenue one, and both targets sit well above Friday's 693.53.
bull: Baird to Outperform with an $800 target and Evercore ISI to Outperform at $813 - both above Friday's 693.53.
25th new 52-week high in twelve months; the trend is intact and confirmed.
Precision agriculture converts machinery sales into recurring software and services revenue.
bear: 1.8% below an all-time high leaves no margin of safety at these levels.
Farm equipment is cyclical and tied to crop prices and farmer credit, both of which soften with higher rates.
Two upgrades at a record high is a crowded-trade signal as much as a bullish one.
DE.inv: A downturn in farm income or a build in dealer inventories would end the equipment cycle regardless of the software story.
DE.thesis: a dominant agricultural equipment franchise with a captive finance arm and a precision-agriculture software layer that is turning a cyclical machinery business into something with recurring revenue. Dealer network and parts create a genuine moat.

DELL.why: A $95bn AI-server backlog - a record, and disclosed rather than forecast - alongside 58% revenue growth and 203% EPS growth. The stock broke a three-month consolidation with a 15.81% single-session move to a 52-week high. This is the clearest evidence in the book that AI capex is being spent rather than announced.
bull: Record $95.0bn AI-server backlog is disclosed revenue, not a forecast.
Q2 FY2027 revenue $47.0bn (+58% y/y) and EPS $7.04 (+203% y/y), with FY guidance raised.
Fox Advisors upgrade to Outperform, $625 target - about 19% above Friday's 524.14.
bear: Server assembly margins are thin; converting backlog into profit is not the same as converting it into revenue.
2.0% below the 52-week high after a 15.81% single-session move - the easy money is gone.
AI-server backlog can be cancelled or deferred; it is an order book, not a contract portfolio.
DELL.inv: If AI-server gross margins compress as the backlog converts, revenue growth will not translate into earnings and the re-rate reverses.
DELL.thesis: AI-server assembly is a lower-margin business than semiconductors, which is the honest caveat - but Dell has the enterprise relationships and the supply-chain scale to convert AI demand into volume nobody else can match. The storage and PC businesses fund the working capital that AI servers consume.

ETN.why: Every AI server in Dell's record $95bn backlog needs power distribution before it does any computing, and Eaton sells that layer with multi-year backlog visibility. It rose 3.46% on Friday against a falling index and still trades 14.0% below its high.
bull: Dell's record $95.0bn AI-server backlog converts directly into demand for Eaton's power distribution.
Rose 3.46% on Friday while the S&P fell 0.38% - industrials was one of three green sectors.
Multi-year backlog gives revenue visibility most industrials do not have.
bear: The reverse-DCF implies roughly high-teens FCF growth is needed - demanding for an industrial.
14.0% below the high means the de-rating has not fully reversed.
Data-centre power orders are the first thing deferred if AI capex slows.
ETN.inv: A slowdown in data-centre orders or backlog cancellations would remove the visibility the multiple depends on.
ETN.thesis: electrical components and power management for data centres, utilities and industrial buildings - the physical layer every AI facility needs before a chip is installed. Trailing FCF of $3.78bn on 388m shares with $0.75bn net cash. Backlog visibility is measured in years.

FISV.why: Rose 0.51% on Friday to 53.00 but trades 61.8% below its 138.62 52-week high and only 12.7% above its 47.04 low. This is the deepest drawdown of any name in the saved list and no base has formed.
bull: Transaction-based revenue is genuinely recurring and grows with nominal consumer spending.
61.8% below the 52-week high - expectations have been reset severely.
Merchant relationships are sticky and expensive to migrate.
bear: 61.8% below the high with only 12.7% of cushion above the low - a falling knife.
No insider cluster and no analyst support in this week's filings.
Competitive pressure on merchant-acquiring take rates is structural, not cyclical.
FISV.inv: A break of the 47.04 52-week low would confirm the de-rating has further to run.
FISV.thesis: Payment processing and merchant acquiring infrastructure - genuinely recurring transaction revenue, currently in a severe de-rating.

FSLR.why: Fell 1.43% on Friday to 204.45 and trades 36.3% below its 320.95 52-week high, just 11.7% above its 182.99 low. Renewables did not participate in Friday's utilities bid (+0.12%) that lifted Constellation 4.88%.
bull: Domestic thin-film manufacturing carries content advantages competitors cannot match.
36.3% below the 52-week high after a sustained policy de-rating.
Backlog extends several years on already-signed contracts.
bear: Did not participate in the utilities bid that lifted CEG 4.88% - the power trade is bypassing solar entirely.
Policy support has reversed and shows no sign of returning.
Only 11.7% above the 52-week low with no base formed.
FSLR.inv: Further policy reversals on domestic-content credits would remove the only structural advantage in the model.
FSLR.thesis: US thin-film solar manufacturing with domestic-content advantages, in a policy environment that has stopped being supportive.

GS.why: An AI IPO window is opening - Anthropic is reported to be preparing a filing - and Goldman is the franchise that monetises it. It trades 10.0% below its 52-week high, a wider discount than JPM, so it offers more repair if capital markets activity picks up.
bull: A reported Anthropic IPO filing would open the highest-fee listing window since 2021.
10.0% below its 52-week high - more repair room than JPM's 2.1%.
Trading revenue benefits from the volatility a coin-flip Fed meeting creates.
bear: Earnings are cyclical and gear to a deal pipeline that can close overnight.
A rate hike in September would likely delay rather than accelerate the IPO calendar.
No smart-money filing supports the name specifically this week.
GS.inv: If the IPO window stays shut through year-end, the capital-markets re-rate does not happen and this is just an expensive rate proxy.
GS.thesis: the premier advisory and trading franchise, now with a far cleaner story than the consumer-banking detour. Earnings are cyclical by design - they gear to deal volume and market volatility rather than to a stable spread - which is a feature when capital markets reopen and a bug when they close.

HTZ.why: Rose 1.32% on Friday to 2.30 but trades 71.9% below its 8.18 52-week high and only 58.6% above its 1.45 low. Consumer discretionary was Friday's worst sector at -1.26% and Brent near $95.73 raises the cost of the fleet's fuel exposure.
bull: 71.9% below the 52-week high.
Rental pricing recovers quickly when travel demand firms.
Rose 1.32% on Friday in a red tape.
bear: Highly leveraged with residual-value exposure it cannot hedge - conviction capped at 1.
Consumer discretionary was Friday's worst sector at -1.26%.
Brent near $95.73 raises fleet operating costs.
HTZ.inv: Falling used-vehicle residuals combined with soft travel demand would threaten the balance sheet directly.
HTZ.thesis: A rental fleet operator whose earnings depend on used-vehicle residual values and on leverage it does not control.

IREN.why: Rose 7.27% on Friday to 44.68 alongside the neocloud complex, and trades 41.9% below its 76.87 52-week high while sitting 76.5% above its 25.31 low.
bull: Rose 7.27% on Friday into a red tape.
Existing power interconnects are the genuinely scarce input for AI data centres.
41.9% below the 52-week high.
bear: Not consistently profitable in the AI segment - conviction capped at 3.
Legacy bitcoin-mining economics still drive part of the P&L and are unrelated to the AI thesis.
Extremely high beta: the 52-week range runs 25.31 to 76.87.
IREN.inv: If AI hosting contracts do not scale, this reverts to being valued as a bitcoin miner.
IREN.thesis: Converting bitcoin-mining data-centre capacity and power contracts into AI compute hosting - the power interconnect is the scarce asset, not the hardware.

ISRG.why: One of the best business models in medical technology - recurring instrument revenue per procedure with multi-year surgeon switching costs - now 39.3% below its high. But nobody inside the company is buying it, and it sits only 11.6% above its 52-week low, so the discount has not yet found a floor.
bull: Recurring instrument revenue per procedure with switching costs measured in surgeon training years.
39.3% below the 52-week high - the multiple compression on a quality franchise has been severe.
Procedure volumes grow with demographics regardless of the economic cycle.
bear: Only 11.6% above the 52-week low and still making lower highs - no base has formed.
Zero insider buying during a 39.3% drawdown is a meaningful absence of confidence.
Competitive robotic platforms from Medtronic and J&J are finally reaching commercial scale.
ISRG.inv: A break of the 328.57 52-week low with procedure growth also decelerating would confirm this is a competitive problem, not a valuation one.
ISRG.thesis: the razor-and-blades model in surgical robotics - systems are placed and the money is made on instruments and accessories per procedure, forever. Surgeon training creates switching costs measured in years. This is a genuinely excellent business.

JPM.why: The hot payroll number that hurt everything else helps this. The 2-year and 5-year both made fresh 52-week highs on Friday and a September hike is now a coin flip - which flows straight into net interest income at the best-capitalised bank in the market. It fell 0.94% to 358.64, only 2.1% off its high.
bull: Front-end yields at fresh 52-week highs feed net interest income directly.
September hike odds near 50% - the rate-geared trade has room if CPI runs hot next week.
Bank-sector insiders are buying: Pinnacle Financial cluster at $99.41, a congressional Fifth Third purchase at $55.10.
bear: Higher-for-longer eventually shows up as consumer credit losses - the rate benefit and the credit cost are the same trade.
2.1% from the record means the rate story is largely in the price.
Trump publicly demanding rate cuts on Friday adds political risk to the Fed path the thesis depends on.
JPM.inv: A credit-cost inflection in the card book, or a sharp dovish turn that flattens the front end, undoes the earnings driver.
JPM.thesis: the best-run large bank in the world, with a deposit franchise, a top-tier investment bank and a card business that each earn independently. Reserve levels and capital ratios give it the ability to buy assets in a downturn rather than sell them.

LULU.why: Collapsed 17.38% on Friday to 100.61 after missing Q3 revenue forecasts, reporting deteriorating comparable sales and cutting its full-year outlook. It now sits 55.5% below its 225.98 52-week high and just 2.7% above its 97.99 52-week low. The reverse-DCF implies negative FCF growth is already priced.
bull: The reverse-DCF implies negative FCF growth - the price already assumes the business shrinks.
55.5% below the 52-week high; expectations have been reset violently.
Brand equity in premium athletic apparel has survived prior demand air-pockets.
bear: Deteriorating comparable sales and a cut full-year outlook - this is a demand problem, not a multiple problem.
Sits 2.7% above the 52-week low with no evidence of a floor.
Consumer discretionary was Friday's worst sector at -1.26%; the sector tape is against it too.
LULU.inv: Another quarter of negative comparable sales confirms structural brand erosion rather than a cyclical dip.
LULU.thesis: A premium athletic-apparel brand in the middle of a genuine demand problem, not a valuation one.

LYFT.why: Fell 3.24% on Friday to 16.72, materially worse than the S&P's 0.38% decline, and trades 34.5% below its 25.54 52-week high. Consumer discretionary was Friday's worst sector at -1.26%.
bull: 34.5% below the 52-week high.
Rideshare demand is resilient and the market is a duopoly.
Cost discipline has improved unit economics from prior years.
bear: Underperformed a weak tape badly on Friday with no news.
Structurally second in a two-player market with less density and no delivery business.
Consumer discretionary was Friday's worst sector at -1.26%.
LYFT.inv: Continued share loss or a price war with the larger competitor removes any path to durable margins.
LYFT.thesis: The number-two US rideshare network, structurally disadvantaged against a larger competitor with more density and a delivery business.

MELI.why: The reverse-DCF prices MercadoLibre for declining free cash flow, which is a strange thing to assume about a business growing marketplace, logistics and fintech simultaneously in under-penetrated markets. The 22.4% drawdown is a dollar story - the 2-year at a fresh 52-week high hurts every emerging-market earner.
bull: The reverse-DCF implies negative FCF growth is priced in - a low bar for a business growing three segments.
22.4% below the 52-week high, driven by currency rather than by operations.
Mercado Pago is now large enough to be valued as a fintech in its own right.
bear: A rising 2-year yield strengthens the dollar and directly compresses Latin American earnings in dollar terms.
Argentine and Brazilian macro volatility is a permanent feature, not a passing risk.
No catalyst and no smart-money support this week.
MELI.inv: A sustained dollar rally alongside decelerating Mercado Pago volumes would break both legs of the thesis at once.
MELI.thesis: three compounding businesses in one - marketplace, logistics and Mercado Pago fintech - across Latin American markets where e-commerce penetration is still low. Trailing FCF of $11.8bn on 51m shares with $5.66bn net cash. The fintech arm is now large enough to matter on its own.

MSFT.why: Broke below $500 on Friday purely because the 5-year yield made a fresh 52-week high - not because anything changed at the company. A 9.8% discount on the most durable cash-flow stream in the market, created by a bond move, is the kind of dislocation worth acting on.
bull: Broke $500 on a bond move, not a business event - the earnings power is unchanged.
Azure plus the OpenAI relationship is the enterprise-AI distribution moat.
9.8% below the 52-week high with $78.2bn net cash and no financing risk.
bear: The reverse-DCF needs roughly 20% annual FCF growth for a decade to justify the price - demanding for a company this size.
The 5-year at a 52-week high keeps compressing high-multiple software regardless of fundamentals.
AI capex is now a large fixed cost; if Azure AI revenue undershoots, margins take the hit.
MSFT.inv: If Azure growth decelerates while AI capex stays elevated, the margin story breaks and the multiple has much further to fall.
MSFT.thesis: the most durable earnings stream in the book. Azure, Office and Windows each throw off cash independently, and the OpenAI relationship gives it a distribution advantage in enterprise AI that no competitor can replicate. Trailing FCF of $72.9bn on 7.43bn shares with $78.2bn net cash.

MU.why: Memory stopped being a commodity this quarter. NAND prices up ~55% q/q and DRAM up 385% y/y with Micron's leading-edge capacity already spoken for through December means the next two prints are largely pre-sold at known prices. The 6.1% Friday gain into a red index is the market working that out.
bull: Leading-edge allocation exhausted through end-2026 means near-term revenue is priced and contracted, not forecast.
NAND up ~70% q/q on volume and ~55% q/q on price - both legs of the cycle are firing at once.
$26.0bn net cash funds the capex response without the equity raise that ended past memory cycles.
bear: Memory has always been cyclical; the same capex that meets this demand creates the 2028 glut.
Up ~9% in a week and ~757% off the 118.52 52-week low - anyone buying here is late to a move, not early to one.
A single hyperscaler trimming an AI-server order changes the allocation math quickly.
MU.inv: If contract DRAM or NAND pricing rolls over q/q, or Micron guides gross margin down, the pricing-power thesis is finished regardless of volume.
MU.thesis: a commodity-cyclical business enjoying the best pricing environment in its history. Trailing FCF of $26.2bn on 1.13bn shares with $26.0bn net cash - a balance sheet that can fund the next capex cycle without dilution, which is not how prior Micron cycles ended.

NBIS.why: Rose 7.48% on Friday to 226.39, one of the strongest sessions on the board, and trades 24.5% below its 299.86 52-week high. It is 258% above its 63.26 low, so this is a high-beta name in a strong but volatile uptrend.
bull: Rose 7.48% on Friday against a falling index.
Neocloud demand rises whenever hyperscaler GPU capacity is constrained - which Micron's sold-out allocation implies it is.
24.5% below the 52-week high with the AI-infrastructure bid returning.
bear: Not consistently profitable - conviction is capped at 3 for that reason.
Up 258% from the 52-week low; extremely high beta in both directions.
Neocloud economics depend on GPU rental rates that hyperscalers can undercut at will.
NBIS.inv: Falling GPU rental rates, or a hyperscaler capacity glut, removes the pricing that makes this model work.
NBIS.thesis: Neocloud GPU capacity rented to AI developers - a leveraged bet on AI compute demand exceeding hyperscaler supply. Not yet consistently profitable.

NCLH.why: Fell 0.13% on Friday to 15.57 and trades 42.7% below its 27.18 52-week high, only 7.2% above its 14.53 low. Brent near $95.73 is a direct cost headwind, and consumer discretionary was Friday's worst sector at -1.26%.
bull: 42.7% below the 52-week high.
Booking curves have historically recovered quickly once fuel costs normalise.
Cruise pricing has held better than the equity implies.
bear: Brent near $95.73 is a direct and material cost increase for a fuel-intensive operator.
Only 7.2% above the 52-week low with the consumer sector leading the market down.
High financial leverage magnifies every operating problem.
NCLH.inv: Sustained Brent above $95 combined with softening bookings would compress margins from both directions.
NCLH.thesis: A leveraged cruise operator whose earnings depend on both consumer discretionary strength and on fuel costs.

NFLX.why: Fell 5.35% on Friday to 78.25, one of the weakest large-cap sessions of the day, and trades 38.2% below its 126.71 52-week high, only 20.2% above its 65.08 low. The reverse-DCF implies roughly 13% annual FCF growth - the least demanding bar in the DCF set.
bull: The reverse-DCF implies only ~13% annual FCF growth is needed - the lowest hurdle of any DCF name here.
38.2% below the 52-week high on a business with genuine global scale.
The advertising tier is a second revenue stream now reaching material size.
bear: Fell 5.35% on Friday with no company news - the tape is against it.
Only 20.2% above the 52-week low; no base has formed.
Content spend competition from Amazon and Apple has no ceiling.
NFLX.inv: A subscriber decline in a developed market alongside falling ad-tier pricing would break both growth legs.
NFLX.thesis: Global streaming with an advertising tier now scaling and content spend that is finally producing operating leverage rather than consuming it.

NOW.why: Down 27.5% from its high on rate pressure rather than business deterioration, and a sitting congressman bought it at $124.00 on Aug 13 as part of a three-name enterprise-software basket. Subscription revenue with high switching costs does not deserve a 27.5% drawdown unless renewals are breaking - and there is no evidence they are.
bull: Rep. Tony Wied bought it at $124.00 on Aug 13 as one of three enterprise-software purchases the same day.
27.5% below the 52-week high with no company-specific bad news behind the fall.
Subscription model with high switching costs - revenue is contracted, not cyclical.
bear: Enterprise software is where AI-disruption fear is concentrated; workflow tools are a plausible target.
The 5-year at a 52-week high keeps compressing every high-multiple subscription name.
A 27.5% drawdown that keeps extending is a trend, and trends are usually right for longer than they should be.
NOW.inv: If renewal rates or net expansion deteriorate in the next print, the drawdown is justified and the value case collapses.
NOW.thesis: the workflow layer enterprises build their operations on, with subscription revenue and renewal rates that make forecasting unusually reliable for software. Switching costs are high because the platform ends up wired into every department.

NVDA.why: Buying the platform layer and the custom-silicon layer at once: Hugging Face for ~$13bn locks in the open-model distribution point, and the $3.5bn MediaTek stake puts NVFusion inside somebody else's custom accelerators. The stock is doing the work - 230.36 into a down tape - which is the problem as much as the point.
bull: Hugging Face gives NVIDIA the default distribution surface for open-weight models, upstream of the chip decision.
The MediaTek/NVFusion deal converts a would-be custom-silicon competitor into a licensee.
Rose 0.84% on a day the S&P fell 0.38% and the Dow fell 0.51% - relative strength into a rate scare.
bear: 2.6% from the 52-week high leaves no margin of safety at these levels.
The 71-72% gross-margin guide from the Aug 26 print still caps the multiple - rising memory costs are Micron's gain and NVIDIA's drag.
A ~$13bn acquisition of a company with modest revenue is a valuation statement the market may not accept.
NVDA.inv: If gross margin guides below ~70% or a hyperscaler discloses a material shift to in-house silicon, the premium multiple is not defensible.
NVDA.thesis: still the reference platform for AI training and inference, with CUDA as the switching cost. Trailing free cash flow of $119.1bn on 24.2bn shares and $53.2bn net cash means it can buy its way into adjacent layers - which it just did.

OKTA.why: Closed at 170.60, up 0.11%, only 2.4% below its 174.85 52-week high - by far the strongest chart in the software sleeve in a week when Zscaler fell 4.5% and ServiceNow fell 2.97%.
bull: Only 2.4% below the 52-week high while the rest of enterprise software de-rates - striking relative strength.
Identity is the security control plane; switching costs are high once deployed.
Held its ground on Friday while high-multiple software sold off.
bear: 2.4% from the high means there is no discount and no margin of safety.
Competition from Microsoft Entra bundled into existing enterprise agreements.
No smart-money filing supports it this week.
OKTA.inv: If Microsoft's bundled identity offering starts winning renewals, the switching-cost moat is smaller than assumed.
OKTA.thesis: Identity and access management - the control plane for enterprise security, with subscription revenue and high switching costs once deployed.

OPEN.why: Rose 0.64% on Friday to 3.15 but sits 71.0% below its 10.87 52-week high and just 4.7% above its 3.01 low. The 10-year at 4.78% and the 5-year at a fresh 52-week high of 4.545% are direct headwinds to housing turnover.
bull: 71.0% below the 52-week high - a very low base if rates ever fall.
Rose 0.64% on Friday in a red tape.
Housing turnover is at cyclical lows and would recover with any rate relief.
bear: Holding houses on a balance sheet while the 5-year makes 52-week highs is the worst possible setup - conviction capped at 1.
4.7% above the 52-week low with the front end still rising.
Not profitable, and the model consumes cash when volumes fall.
OPEN.inv: Any further rise in mortgage rates deepens the inventory losses; this only works if rates fall.
OPEN.thesis: Algorithmic home buying and selling - a balance-sheet-intensive model in the most rate-sensitive industry there is.

OSCR.why: Closed effectively flat at 32.25 (+0.03%) and sits only 3.9% below its 33.55 52-week high - remarkable relative strength in a week when healthcare was Friday's second-worst sector at -1.04%.
bull: Only 3.9% below the 52-week high while healthcare as a sector fell 1.04% on Friday.
Up 202% from the 10.69 52-week low - the turnaround has been validated by the tape.
Lower administrative cost structure than legacy insurers.
bear: 3.9% from the high leaves no margin of safety after a 202% run.
Small insurers are the most exposed to medical loss ratio surprises.
Regulatory and risk-adjustment changes hit sub-scale insurers hardest.
OSCR.inv: A medical loss ratio miss would show the technology advantage does not offset the lack of scale.
OSCR.thesis: Technology-driven health insurer competing on member experience and cost of administration rather than on scale.

SHEL.why: Morgan Stanley upgraded Shell to Overweight from Equal Weight on Friday and raised the target to $101.30 from $81.60. It closed at 92.95, up 0.67%, just 2.1% below its 94.90 52-week high, with Brent up more than 8% on the week.
bull: Morgan Stanley upgrade to Overweight with the target lifted to $101.30 from $81.60 - a 24% target raise.
Largest LNG trading book globally, the best asset to hold through a gas and crude dislocation.
Rose 0.67% on Friday while energy as a sector fell 0.98%.
bear: 2.1% from the 52-week high - most of the upgrade is already in the price.
Entirely dependent on the Hormuz disruption persisting.
European majors carry political and windfall-tax risk US peers do not.
SHEL.inv: A negotiated Hormuz reopening collapses both the LNG and crude legs of the thesis.
SHEL.thesis: An integrated major with the largest LNG trading book in the world - which is the asset that monetises a Hormuz supply dislocation better than any barrel of crude.

SKHY.why: Rose 8.14% on Friday to 177.00, one of the strongest sessions on the board, alongside Micron's 6.1% and SanDisk's 11.9%. It trades 9.1% below its 194.80 52-week high - the least discounted of the memory names, which is what leadership looks like.
bull: Rose 8.14% on Friday while the S&P fell 0.38%.
Leading position in high-bandwidth memory, the highest-value memory product in an AI rack.
DRAM market grew 385% y/y in Q2 2026 - the pricing environment is unprecedented.
bear: Only 9.1% below the 52-week high - the least discounted memory name here.
Memory is cyclical; the capex response to this pricing creates the next glut.
ADR liquidity and Korean market hours make execution imprecise.
SKHY.inv: A q/q decline in DRAM contract pricing ends the memory trade across all three names at once.
SKHY.thesis: The other leg of the memory oligopoly, with the leading position in high-bandwidth memory for AI accelerators.

SLB.why: Services is the delayed-fuse way to own $95 Brent: operators set budgets on the strip, so a sustained high price shows up in SLB's 2027 order book rather than this quarter's. It closed at 57.51, up a token 0.17%, having already run to within 4.9% of its high.
bull: Sustained $95 Brent flows into 2027 operator capex budgets, which is SLB's revenue.
International and offshore mix insulates it from US shale volatility.
Digital revenue is a higher-margin, recurring layer the market still values as a services multiple.
bear: Services lag the barrel by quarters - a de-escalation before budget season means the money never arrives.
Already within 4.9% of the 52-week high after a strong run; the easy repair is done.
Operators have been disciplined this cycle - high prices no longer automatically mean high activity.
SLB.inv: If operators hold capex flat through a $95 Brent tape, the activity thesis fails no matter what the barrel does.
SLB.thesis: the largest oilfield services company, earning on activity rather than on the barrel directly, with an international and offshore mix that is less exposed to US shale's boom-bust than the domestic pressure-pumpers. Digital and production-optimisation revenue is the higher-margin, stickier layer.

SMCI.why: Rose 4.54% on Friday to 39.59 but trades 32.6% below its 58.78 52-week high, and it conspicuously did not participate in Dell's +15.81% breakout week. Dell disclosed a $95.0bn AI-server backlog; SMCI has disclosed nothing comparable.
bull: Rose 4.54% on Friday with the AI-hardware complex.
Liquid-cooling expertise is a genuine differentiator as rack density rises.
32.6% below the 52-week high.
bear: Did not participate in Dell's breakout week - it is losing the orders Dell is winning.
Governance and filing history keeps a permanent valuation discount attached.
Server assembly margins are thin and competition is intensifying.
SMCI.inv: Continued share loss to Dell in AI-server orders makes the discount permanent rather than temporary.
SMCI.thesis: AI server assembly with liquid-cooling expertise, competing directly with Dell for the same rack orders - but with a governance history that keeps a discount attached.

SMR.why: Fell 0.51% on Friday to 9.70 while Constellation rose 4.88% and Vistra 3.52%. It trades 83.1% below its 57.42 52-week high and only 34.5% above its 7.21 low. The nuclear bid this week went entirely to operating fleets, not to future ones.
bull: SMR technology remains the only credible path to new nuclear capacity this decade.
83.1% below the 52-week high - expectations have been almost entirely reset.
Data-centre power demand is the natural customer base.
bear: Pre-revenue - conviction capped at 2. There is no cash flow to value.
Fell on a day the operating nuclear fleets rose 3-5%; the market is separating real megawatts from future ones.
First commercial deployment remains years away with regulatory milestones outstanding.
SMR.inv: Any further regulatory or schedule slippage on first deployment pushes the cash-flow date beyond the investable horizon.
SMR.thesis: Small modular reactor developer - a pre-revenue story on a technology whose first commercial deployment is still years out.

SNDK.why: Surged 11.9% on Friday to 1,740.00 - the biggest move on the board - while the S&P fell 0.38%. Lynx Research published a $2,450 target the same day. It remains 26.1% below its 2,354.39 52-week high.
bull: NAND prices up ~55% q/q with volumes up ~70% q/q - both legs of the cycle firing.
Rose 11.9% on Friday into a red index.
Lynx Research $2,450 target implies roughly 41% upside from 1,740.00.
bear: Pure-play NAND has no diversification when the cycle turns - and it always turns.
The 52-week low of 55.55 shows how violent this stock's range is; position size accordingly.
A parabolic move into a $2,450 target is the kind of setup that reverses hard.
SNDK.inv: Any q/q decline in NAND contract pricing ends this trade immediately.
SNDK.thesis: Pure-play NAND flash at the sharpest point of the memory pricing cycle. NAND market volume grew 70% q/q with prices up about 55% q/q in Q2 2026.

SOFI.why: Fell 1.57% on Friday to 18.22, underperforming the S&P's 0.38% decline, and trades 44.3% below its 32.73 52-week high. A rising front end - the 2-year at a fresh 52-week high of 4.374% - raises funding costs for a lender like this.
bull: Fee-based revenue is growing faster than the lending book, improving earnings quality.
44.3% below the 52-week high - substantial repair room if credit holds.
Bank-charter funding is cheaper than the warehouse lines it replaced.
bear: Underperformed a weak tape on Friday with no news.
The 2-year at a 52-week high raises funding costs directly.
Consumer credit is the entire risk and it deteriorates late in a hiking cycle.
SOFI.inv: Rising personal-loan charge-offs would show the credit box was too wide during the growth phase.
SOFI.thesis: A digital bank and lending platform with a growing fee-based segment, but earnings quality still depends on credit performance.

SYM.why: Rose 3.22% on Friday to 42.94 as industrials advanced 0.22%, but it trades 51.1% below its 87.88 52-week high and only 14.0% above its 37.68 low - the weakest chart in the industrials group here.
bull: Rose 3.22% on Friday with the industrials bid.
Warehouse automation demand is structural as labour costs rise.
51.1% below the 52-week high.
bear: Extreme customer concentration in Walmart - conviction capped at 3.
Only 14.0% above the 52-week low; the downtrend is intact.
Deployment revenue recognition has been lumpy and has caused prior guidance misses.
SYM.inv: Any change in the Walmart deployment schedule would remove the majority of the revenue visibility.
SYM.thesis: Warehouse automation robotics with a large Walmart deployment - customer concentration is both the growth engine and the central risk.

TE.why: Rose 1.32% on Friday to 4.60 but trades 63.2% below its 12.49 52-week high. First Solar, the established domestic manufacturer, fell 1.43% the same day and did not participate in the utilities bid - the renewables complex was left behind entirely this week.
bull: 63.2% below the 52-week high.
Domestic manufacturing content carries policy advantages where support exists.
Rose 1.32% on Friday in a red tape.
bear: Pre-scale and capital intensive - conviction capped at 1.
The whole renewables complex was bypassed by Friday's utilities bid.
Policy support for domestic solar has reversed.
TE.inv: Failure to reach manufacturing scale before capital runs short is the binary risk here.
TE.thesis: Domestic solar manufacturing scale-up - a capital-intensive build in a policy environment that has turned hostile.

TSM.why: The chokepoint. Every AI revenue number disclosed this week - Broadcom's $58bn FY26 AI guide, Dell's $95bn server backlog, Micron's sold-out allocation - has to pass through TSMC's leading-edge fabs. Three insiders bought the Taiwan line on Aug 18 and the ADR still trades 10.5% below its high.
bull: Monopoly at the leading edge - no substitute exists for 2nm-class capacity at volume.
Three insiders bought the Taiwan line on Aug 18, adding ~36% to their holdings.
$110.6bn net cash funds the fab build-out with no financing risk.
bear: Taiwan Strait risk is unhedgeable and unpriceable; one headline re-rates the whole position.
Customer concentration in a handful of AI buyers whose capex is discretionary.
US fab expansion runs at structurally lower margins than the Taiwan base.
TSM.inv: A material Taiwan Strait escalation, or a leading-edge capacity glut from over-building, breaks the monopoly premium.
TSM.thesis: a genuine monopoly at the leading edge. Everything in this book that ships an AI chip - NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, Apple - is fabricated here. Trailing FCF of $35.3bn with $110.6bn net cash on 4.67bn ADS, and pricing power that is now being exercised rather than merely possessed.

UA.why: Rose 0.39% on Friday to 5.12 and trades 35.2% below its 7.91 52-week high. The relevant read-across is Lululemon's 17.38% collapse on deteriorating comparable sales - if the premium end of athletic apparel is weakening, the value end has less room to take share than the turnaround assumes.
bull: 35.2% below the 52-week high on a recognised global brand.
Rose 0.39% on Friday while consumer discretionary fell 1.26%.
Inventory and channel cleanup is largely complete.
bear: Lululemon's 17.38% collapse on deteriorating comps signals category weakness, not just company weakness.
Consumer discretionary was Friday's worst sector at -1.26%.
Brand repositioning has been attempted repeatedly without durable success.
UA.inv: Category-wide athletic apparel weakness removes the share-gain opportunity the turnaround depends on.
UA.thesis: A turnaround in a brand that lost its position in premium athletic apparel and is trying to rebuild it.

VLO.why: The cleanest way to own the Hormuz disruption. Tanker transits through the strait have fallen 77% from pre-war levels, which dislocates crude-to-product flows and widens crack spreads - exactly what a Gulf Coast refiner monetises. It made a new 52-week high this week and closed at 370.72.
bull: Hormuz throughput down 77% from Q4 2025 levels - the physical dislocation is measurable and ongoing.
Brent +8% on the week to ~$95.73 with war-risk insurance at multi-year highs.
Fresh 52-week high this week - the tape is confirming the fundamental, not fighting it.
bear: This is entirely a geopolitical trade; a ceasefire headline takes the crack spread and the stock down together.
Refining margins mean-revert hard and fast once supply normalises.
1.2% from the 52-week high means you are buying at the top of the range.
VLO.inv: A negotiated reopening of Hormuz collapses crack spreads and voids the thesis inside a week.
VLO.thesis: a pure refiner with no exploration risk - it earns the crack spread between crude in and product out. Low-cost Gulf Coast complexity means it captures widening spreads faster than peers. The trade-off is that this is a margin business with no recurring revenue.

VRT.why: AI racks run hot enough that cooling content per rack is growing faster than rack count, and Vertiv supplies it. Dell just disclosed a record $95bn AI-server backlog. VRT rose 4.35% on Friday into a red tape and still sits 26.2% below its high.
bull: Cooling content per rack rises with AI rack density - the addressable market grows faster than unit volume.
Dell's record $95.0bn AI-server backlog is direct, disclosed demand.
Rose 4.35% on Friday against a falling index.
bear: 26.2% below the high - this name has bounced and failed repeatedly through the AI-infrastructure de-rating.
High beta to AI capex sentiment with no valuation floor and no smart-money support.
Competition in liquid cooling is intensifying as the market becomes obviously large.
VRT.inv: A book-to-bill below 1.0 would mean orders are no longer keeping pace and the growth multiple is unsupportable.
VRT.thesis: data-centre cooling and power infrastructure - a business whose addressable market expands mechanically with rack density. AI servers run hotter than anything before them, so the cooling content per rack is rising faster than rack count.

VST.why: The same structural thesis as Constellation at roughly 14.4x forward earnings versus 22.4x, with 2,609MW of 20-year Meta agreements including 433MW of new capacity that comes from upgrading plants it already owns rather than building new ones. It bounced 3.52% on Friday off a deep base.
bull: Roughly 14.4x forward earnings against Constellation's 22.4x for a comparable AI-power thesis.
2,609MW of 20-year Meta agreements, with 433MW coming from upgrades rather than new build.
Up 12.5% from the 132.66 August low and +3.52% on Friday against a red index.
bear: No insider or congressional support at all - nobody with an edge is buying this here.
32.1% below the 52-week high; the downtrend is intact until proven otherwise.
A merchant power fleet is exposed to gas prices and capacity-auction outcomes it does not control.
VST.inv: A break below the 132.66 52-week low would confirm the de-rating has further to run and the base has failed.
VST.thesis: a nuclear and gas fleet with 2,609MW of 20-year Meta agreements including 433MW of new capacity from upgrades at existing plants - growth without greenfield construction risk. It trades near 14.4x forward earnings, materially cheaper than Constellation's 22.4x.

VSTS.why: Rose 5.74% on Friday to 13.26, driven primarily by a major open-market share purchase by President and CEO James J. Barber. It trades 21.5% below its 16.90 52-week high but is 233% above its 3.98 low - the turnaround is already substantially priced.
bull: The sitting CEO bought a major open-market stake - the highest-quality single-insider signal available.
Route-based uniform rental is genuinely recurring revenue with high customer retention.
Rose 5.74% on Friday while the S&P fell 0.38%.
bear: Up 233% from the 52-week low of 3.98 - most of the turnaround repair has happened.
A small-cap with limited liquidity; exits are harder than entries.
One CEO purchase does not make a cluster.
VSTS.inv: If route revenue or customer retention deteriorates in the next print, the CEO was buying a story rather than a turn.
VSTS.thesis: Uniform rental and workplace supplies - a boring recurring-revenue route business trading at a fraction of its former value after an operational reset.

XOM.why: Brent rose more than 8% on the week and Exxon fell 1.69% on Friday, leaving it 9.6% below its 52-week high. The integrated model means it earns on both the crude and the refining leg of the Hormuz dislocation, and you are buying it at a discount to where the barrel says it should be.
bull: Integrated structure earns on both the crude leg and the refining leg of the Hormuz supply shock.
Fell 1.69% Friday while Brent held ~$95.73 - a gap that historically closes.
9.6% below the 52-week high with $8.4bn net cash and a dividend management will not cut.
bear: The equity's refusal to follow the barrel may be the market pricing an end to the conflict premium.
Reverse-DCF requires roughly mid-teens FCF growth from an integrated major - a demanding bar.
Energy was Friday's third-worst sector at -0.98% despite the oil move; the rotation is not with it.
XOM.inv: If the equity keeps de-rating while Brent holds above $90, the market is telling you something about long-run demand that the barrel is not - respect it.
XOM.thesis: an integrated with upstream, refining and chemicals under one roof, which smooths the cycle that hits pure E&Ps and pure refiners. Trailing FCF of $18.8bn on 4.14bn shares with $8.4bn net cash, and a dividend record management treats as inviolable.
